system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The overall structure of the prompt mimics the structure of the program skeleton, with the following differences
system_prompt_style.note: The prompt is built per sample from the skeleton plus k=2 sampled programs; there is no separate system prompt. Sampled programs change every call, so dynamically_composed is also arguable.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: We believe that the LLM used within FunSearch does not use much context about the problem
env_context_strategy.note: Context is only the skeleton and the sampled programs; there is no environment navigation. Paper-only evidence.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no code bundle. Each prompt is freshly built, so no history accumulates.

observation_format.evidence_quote: These programs are then combined into a single prompt
observation_format.note: The model sees program text; evaluator scores go to the database, not the model.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: a priority v2 function with no body is appended — the LLM will be in charge of completing the body of that function
tool_call_format.note: The completed function is executed by the evaluators.

tool_count.note: No tool list is available in the evidence; the model only completes code.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: a priority v2 function with no body is appended — the LLM will be in charge of completing the body of that function
edit_primitive.note: Closest value: the model rewrites the whole evolved function, not a file.

protocol_standardization.note: Paper only; no dependency list or source was available to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: an evolutionary procedure based on pairing a pre-trained LLM with a system
loop_primitives.note: Evolutionary search is not in the value list. Coded as the closest values: LLM sampling scored by an evaluator over a program database. This is an ambiguity case.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the LLM should instead be seen as a source of diverse (syntactically correct) programs
planning_granularity.note: Paper only; no planning step is described.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: three types of workers: a programs database, samplers, and evaluators, which communicate asynchronously
multi_agent_topology.note: Multiple sampler workers run the same LLM; they are distributed workers, not a multi-agent system.

human_in_loop.note: The paper describes humans refining the search between runs (Sec. 2.1), not an in-run gating mechanism.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The programs database keeps a population of correct programs, which are then sampled to create prompts.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Programs generated by the LLM are evaluated and scored on a set of inputs.
self_verification.note: Closest value: a harness-run evaluate function scores programs, rather than tests.

retry_policy.note: Evolution samples continuously; the paper does not define task-level retry.

termination_condition.note: The paper says 'repeated until termination' without specifying the condition.

timeouts.evidence_quote: did not execute within the imposed time and memory limits
timeouts.note: Time limit applies to each program evaluation.

execution_isolation.note: The paper mentions an internal sandbox that is not part of the release; there is no code evidence for the shipped version.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models

open_source.evidence_quote: a single-threaded implementation of theFunSearchpipeline are available as Python code
open_source.note: The distributed system and sandbox are not released. The licence was not available to verify.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: the results obtained in this paper are not too sensitive to the exact choice of LLM
model_agnostic.note: Codey and StarCoder were both used.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: a single-threaded implementation of theFunSearchpipeline are available as Python code in the Supplementary information
primary_artifact.note: The repo appears frozen to the paper.

first_release_date.note: No tag or commit information; the paper was accepted 2023-11-30.
